answer: A tide is locked into a mirror only while that mirror faces the forge during the firing. The silver keeps the waterline and the facing together, so a later copy of the words has a waterline and no facing. A second key that repeats the tide is showing a picture of a firing it did not attend. A second mirror fired in that same forge while facing the same basin takes the same waterline, and that second facing does not raise another tide. A mirror turned away after the firing stays dark, because the forge writes the tide only into silver that is facing it.
